chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Hank Jones, Oscar Peterson and Phineas Newborn
summary: Jackson calls Hank Jones the complete pianist with a fine tone and rates Oscar Peterson and Phineas Newborn close to Tatum.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So we was speaking, still speaking about pianists, wasn't we? I was thinking about Benny Payne.
Yeah.
What a great accompanist he was.
Uh-huh. And Hank Jones? What about --
Hank Jones to me -- there's nothing you can say about Hank too much. Hank is one of the most --
He's the epitome of pianists.

That's right, full-fledged pianist. Any kind of piano you want, any kind of piano you want, Hank Jones can play it. I don't care -- If you want him to even go back to 1915, he can play that. Up till now, if you want him to play a vant-gark, he can play that.
Whatever.
It doesn't make any difference. And I love his sound on the piano. There are certain guys that get a tone out of a piano. He gets a tone -- artistic
Which is really (inaudible)?
Yeah, Art got a tone out of the piano, to me.
Right.
And --
The piano, being a pluckless instrument where you just strike it, it takes quite some doing to --
Oscar Peterson to me is another pianist that -- oh, I can name you pianists that -- and Phineas Newborn.
Oh, yeah.

Phineas Newborn, of the young pianists, to me is the greatest, of the young pianists. Of course, he's younger than Oscar and the guys that came up in the Art Tatum era, you know. Of course, Oscar's a little later than Art

Tatum. But to me, I put Oscar right there, you know, in that category just about, you see. Not as great as Art because nobody to me would ever be as great as Art. But he's up in that category. And Phineas Newborn, too, to me is about up in that category.
Right. Where does he live now? In California someplace?
In California, yeah.
Yeah.
You know, he had problems.
He had a nervous breakdown or something.
Yes, he did, yeah. But I have records of his, of him at home.
Oh, yes.
Shew, beautiful.
I made some records with him.
Uh-huh.
